# Voice-first generated video

**Use when** the film will be generated by a video model from a locked voiceover: illustrated or animated
explainers where the model may choose staging and camera. The shortest path from a locked voiceover to a
watchable film.
**Do not use** when no video-model spend is authorized (use [stills-first](../stills-first/RECIPE.md)), when the
picture must show real product UI or exact figures (use a code-rendered style), or to compare looks cheaply
(use [style peg](../style-peg/RECIPE.md) or stills).
The starter is [`starter/`](starter/README.md): the prompt template and the step list with a dry run.

Proven on the September 2026 AlphaGenome "Rooms" film (Seedance 2.5 on fal.ai): 69 seconds, three text-only
generations, no reference images, about $33 of video, the best result of every path tried. Use the video model
version the profile or brief names; never silently fall back to an older version.

## The path

1. **Voice script, locked and recorded.** Unchanged from the other modes: record it with the key-gated
   `vo.py` in the [vo-explainer starter](../vo-explainer/starter/README.md). The recorded
   read with real timings is the spine; nothing below happens without it.
2. **Scene brief, one page of text.** Three parts, written against the recording:
   - a *style paragraph*: medium, ground colour, fills, line, the accent colours and
     what each one is reserved for, what is forbidden (gradients, 3D, photo look,
     lettering);
   - a *world paragraph*: the metaphor and its vocabulary, each recurring object named
     once with what it stands for, and who may appear where;
   - a *beat table*: for every voice sentence or pair, the time range, the narrator's
     words, and one sentence saying what the picture must make clear.
   This is the direction work. The stills phase used to force it; now it is written.
3. **Generate straight from the brief.** Split at sentence boundaries into parts of at
   most the model's ceiling (30 s on Seedance 2.5). Each part gets the style and world
   paragraphs verbatim plus its beats. Send the parts in parallel; they do not share
   frames.
4. **Review from frames, then watch.** Scene-cut detection, a 1 fps contact sheet, a
   handful of full-size key frames. Then lay the real voice over each part and watch
   at speed. Say which of those you did.
5. **Stitch and ship a rough.** Concat the narrated parts. Send it with the parts.
6. **Reference pass only if something drifted.** Palette, a character, a prop. Bind a
   few approved stills and rerun the same prompt. Do not start here.

Stills are optional in this mode. They keep two jobs: choosing between aesthetic
directions when the look is not settled (eleven stills per direction beats a $14
video per direction), and supplying references for step 6. A dense 1–2 fps stills
animatic is not needed and should not be built before video.

## The prompt shape that worked, and the one that did not

Per shot, give only: the time range, the narrator's line, what must be clear, and
where the cuts fall. Set style and world once at the top. Let the model choose
staging, actions and camera.

Do not script gestures ("the hand touches the tile, lifts it, studies it, returns it
to the same slot") or camera moves per shot. The choreographed take executed every
instruction and the choreographed beats were its weakest; the one shot described as a
state and a mood was its best. The voice-first rerun of the same 30 seconds fixed the
palette, staged its own reveal on the key line, and pulled back from one silhouette to
a hall of empty doorways without being asked. The rule that came out of it: tell the model what the
voice-over says at each point, tell it where the cuts are, and leave the rest to it.

Reserve explicit action direction for a retake in which one specific beat failed.
One variable per retake.

Template: [`starter/VOICE-FIRST-PROMPT.template.md`](starter/VOICE-FIRST-PROMPT.template.md).

## Splitting the voice

Cut at sentence ends, never at a round number. A 69 s track with breaks at 30.17 and
53.91 s became 30 + 24 + 16 s parts, not 30 + 30 + 9. Pad each voice segment to its
part's container length with silence and a short fade so the mux is exact; the stitch
then runs a second or so longer than the track, which is fine for a rough.

```
ffmpeg -ss 30.170 -to 53.910 -i vo.wav -af "apad=whole_dur=24,afade=t=out:st=23.6:d=0.4" part2-vo.wav
ffmpeg -i part2.mp4 -i part2-vo.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac -shortest part2-narrated.mp4
ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i parts.txt -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -c:a aac full-rough.mp4
```

## What the model did well and where it drifted (Seedance 2.5, text only, 720p)

Held: shot count and cut timing within a second of the brief; a flat 2D medium once
named as "hand-drawn 2D animation, flat screenprint" with no lens vocabulary; every
beat's required meaning; a stable character across the shots it appeared in; morphing
between beats where the brief allowed it (rings fracturing into a mosaic of rooms,
architecture folding into book pages).

Drifted: a reserved accent colour spread to other objects; soft glow crept into one
corridor; props outside the palette (wooden vessels rendered brown); a robe reduced to
a contour; a singular comparison ("one wider opening next to ours") rendered as a
repeated row. These are what a reference pass is for.

On a 3D stop-motion look, text only held six shots and five cuts too, but drifted on
prop inventory (six tiles for four, a mug for a tumbler, a reinterpreted model).

## Submitting

[`scripts/seedance_gen.py`](../../scripts/seedance_gen.py) `part1 part2` reads `prompt.txt` and `spec.json` from each directory,
submits sequentially, polls, downloads `raw.mp4`, writes a frame sheet and logs the estimated
cost. `--dry-run` writes `payload.json` and prints the plan and estimated cost without uploading or submitting,
and needs no key and no `fal_client`; see [`starter/README.md`](starter/README.md). Schema, prices, client calls and the error shape are in
[fal-seedance-25-api.md](../../references/fal-seedance-25-api.md).

## Cost and filter facts, dated 2026-09-11

fal.ai `bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`, displayed rates: 480p $0.2205/s,
720p $0.473/s, 1080p $1.164/s. A 30 s 720p take is about $14.19; the 69 s Rooms rough
was about $33. Inference ran 9–16 minutes per part. Billing is token-based; treat
these as estimates and read the dashboard. A non-admin fal key gets 403 from the
billing and FOCUS endpoints, so state the estimate and say it is unverified.

Rejected submissions (HTTP 422 `content_policy_violation`, `partner_validation_failed`)
return before generation and appear not to bill. The partner filter rejected a set of
stylised 3D stills that showed no person, not even a hand; the same pipeline accepted
flat 2D stills with human silhouettes and an anatomical figure. The one difference
found was DNA-helix imagery in every rejected still and none in the accepted ones.
Untested hypothesis, recorded so the next session does not re-derive it. Text-only
generation sidesteps the image filter entirely.

## Approved reference

The AlphaGenome "Rooms" text-to-video rough, `rooms-t2v-full-rough.mp4` (70.17 s stitched, three parts).
Recorded verdicts, quoted from the files:

- `~/cs/films/daimon-alphagenome-film/explore/round2/seedance25-ladder/REVIEW-t2v-full.md`:
  "Best material so far. The VO-first prompt shape works across all three parts." It also lists the fix list for
  a reference pass and says "Full-speed smoothness not reviewed on any part; frame-sampled only."
- `~/cs/films/daimon-alphagenome-film/PAUSED-HANDOFF.md` (2026-09-11 resume section): the
  director's rule after rung 1b, "prompt = VO line + cuts per shot".

No final-film approval is recorded; the next step written there is a reference pass for palette drift.
